title: Unpack Nordic countries safely
description:
names = ['Finland', 'Sweden', 'Norway','Denmark','Iceland', 'Estonia','Russia']. Unpack the first five countries and store them in a variable nordic_countries, store Estonia and Russia in es, and ru respectively.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `unpack_countries(names)`, using starred unpacking (`*nordic_countries, es, ru = names`) so that, for any list of country names passed in, every item except the last two is collected into nordic_countries and the last two items go into es and ru, returning the tuple `(nordic_countries, es, ru)`. Because this day's topic is exception handling, if names has fewer than two elements the unpacking raises a ValueError - catch it internally and return a descriptive string instead of letting it propagate.
examples:
>>> unpack_countries(['Finland', 'Sweden', 'Norway', 'Denmark', 'Iceland', 'Estonia', 'Russia'])
(['Finland', 'Sweden', 'Norway', 'Denmark', 'Iceland'], 'Estonia', 'Russia')
>>> unpack_countries(['OnlyOne'])
'Unpacking error: not enough values to unpack (expected at least 2, got 1)'
starter_code:
def unpack_countries(names):
    # write your code here
    # unpack names so every item except the last two goes into
    # nordic_countries, and the last two go into es and ru
    # catch the ValueError raised when names has fewer than 2 items
    pass
hints: Python can unpack a list into several variables in one assignment, and a starred variable (like *rest) scoops up 'everything else' into a list while plain variables take the remaining ends of the sequence.
The pattern `*nordic_countries, es, ru = names` puts every element of names except the last two into nordic_countries as a list, then assigns the last two elements to es and ru.

When names has fewer than two elements that unpacking raises a ValueError ('not enough values to unpack') - wrap the unpacking line in a try/except ValueError block and return a descriptive string from the except branch instead of letting the exception crash the program.
expected_behavior: Returns a 3-tuple (nordic_countries, es, ru) where nordic_countries is a list of every element of names except the last two, es is the second-to-last element, and ru is the last element. If names has fewer than two elements, the ValueError raised by the unpacking is caught internally and a descriptive error string ('Unpacking error: ' followed by the exception message) is returned instead of raising.

hidden_tests.label: source example: seven countries split into nordic_countries, es, ru
exactly two elements: nordic_countries is empty

hidden_tests.expected: 'Unpacking error: not enough values to unpack (expected at least 2, got 1)'
hidden_tests.label: exception path: single-element list caught and reported

hidden_tests.expected: 'Unpacking error: not enough values to unpack (expected at least 2, got 0)'
hidden_tests.label: exception path: empty list caught and reported

explanation: Starred assignment (`*nordic_countries, es, ru = names`) unpacks a sequence by first reserving the last two positions for es and ru, then collecting everything else into the nordic_countries list. This only works if names has at least two items to fill es and ru; otherwise Python raises a ValueError describing how many values it needed versus how many it got. Wrapping the unpacking in try/except ValueError lets the function handle that failure gracefully and hand back a descriptive string instead of crashing, which is exactly the graceful-exit idiom this lesson introduces.
